# Air Alarms An air alarm is a device that lets you centrally monitor and control every atmospheric device linked to it.
It allows an atmospheric technician to manage the atmosphere in a given area quickly and efficiently.
Rooms often have a wall-mounted air alarm for quickly controlling several devices inside them.
The guide on [textlink="networking" link="Networking"] explains how to link devices.
## User interface Interacting with an air alarm opens a menu with 3 sections: - Top: the air alarm's current status. This displays the current pressure and temperature of the area it monitors. - Middle: lists of linked [textlink="air vents" link="AirVent"] and [textlink="air scrubbers" link="AirScrubber"], as well as every sensor sending data to the alarm. - Bottom: buttons for controlling the air alarm's operating modes and a toggle for automatic mode switching.
## Alarm status Air alarms quickly communicate the state of the monitored area through the color of the device's indicator: - [color=green]Normal[/color]: the air in the area is safe to breathe. - [color=yellow]Warning[/color]: the area's atmosphere is beginning to deviate from the desired values and is becoming unsafe. - [color=red]Danger[/color]: the area is no longer safe; internals or spacesuits are required.
Air alarms automatically lower linked [textlink="firelocks" link="FireAndGasControl"] when the status reaches [color=Red]Danger[/color]. These [textlink="firelocks" link="FireAndGasControl"] automatically rise when the status returns to [color=green]Normal[/color].
Air alarms have [textlink="signal" link="Networking"] outputs for each of the three statuses. They can be used to activate other [textlink="signal" link="Networking"] devices when the status changes.
## Sensors All [textlink="air vents" link="AirVent"] and [textlink="air scrubbers" link="AirScrubber"] have a built-in sensor that sends data to the air alarm. These sensors can be configured in the [bold]Sensors[/bold] tab of the air alarm menu.
The air alarm's status is determined directly by each sensor's thresholds. If a sensor reports pressure, temperature, or gas composition outside the configured thresholds, the air alarm will change its status.
These thresholds can be adjusted or disabled as needed. For example, if you are monitoring a room with a naturally low temperature, such as a freezer, or a high temperature, such as a combustion chamber, you can adjust the temperature thresholds to the expected values.
You can also build an air sensor and [textlink="link it" link="Networking"] to an air alarm.
This is useful for monitoring areas that do not yet have an air vent or scrubber.
## Operating modes To control connected devices quickly, air alarms have operating modes that change the behavior of every linked device to achieve the desired effect. - None: disables every device linked to the air alarm. - Filtering: enables [textlink="air vents" link="AirVent"] with their external bound set to standard atmospheric pressure. [textlink="Air scrubbers" link="AirScrubber"] are enabled and normally remove all waste gases. - Filtering (Wide): the same as Filtering, but every linked [textlink="air scrubber" link="AirScrubber"] enables WideNet mode. - Fill: enables [textlink="air vents" link="AirVent"] with their external bound set to the maximum pressure of [color=orange][protodata="GasVentPump" comp="GasVentPump" member="MaxPressure"/] kPa[/color]. [textlink="Air scrubbers" link="AirScrubber"] are disabled. - Panic: disables [textlink="air vents" link="AirVent"] and switches [textlink="air scrubbers" link="AirScrubber"] to siphoning mode.
Air alarms automatically switch between Filtering and Filtering (Wide) depending on the area's current status. - If the area reaches [color=red]Danger[/color] status or higher, the air alarm switches to Filtering (Wide). - If the area reaches [color=green]Normal[/color] or [color=yellow]Warning[/color] status, the air alarm switches to Filtering.
This behavior can be disabled by clearing the "Auto" checkbox in the bottom section of the air alarm menu.
Useful advice for dealing with [textlink="depressurization" link="Spacing"] and [textlink="fires" link="Fires"] can be found in their respective guides.
